title: The old black Carnival downtown
summary: He recalls the Carnival on Claiborne and the streets around it and wishes it had been filmed.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: We're up to reel number seven. We're up to number seven on Tommy Ridgler. Okay, and we're talking about Carnival and how it's changed.

Oh yeah, well, what I was talking about, the Black Carnival downtown on Arlene Street. You see, I mean, from Arlene and Claiborne on down to Arlene and St. Bernard, this was a Carnival, and then on Melford, I never did go on Melford Mean Street from, well, it's Martin Luther King now, from Claiborne on down to Dry. I never did go in that direction. I always went down and down. And from there, I walked Claiborne Street, and then I would go on Connell Street. But, you know, I wish some people had filmed that era of Carnival, and in a way you could see it. It was fantastic. It was really fantastic. It was something to see there. You know, a lot of things, Carnival now leave a lot to be desired. That's why Carnival's not as big with me as it gives me. You know how Carnival is big with me? How many gigs I can get. How many Carnival balls I can play. See, last year.
